y-m-41-05.goal: Predict matrix-power rule, update prediction and confidence with new calculations; judge whether rule for one matrix transfers to another.
y-m-41-05.material: A is 2×2 with rows (0,−1),(1,0). E identity rows (1,0),(0,1); −E changes all signs. A²=A×A; A³=A²×A. As facts reveal stepwise, revise prediction for repeated powers. [2 2 0 1 1 0 1 0 0 1]

y-m-41-05.s.s1.st.0.after: A³=A²A=(−E)A=−A; A⁴=A²A²=(−E)(−E)=E. Reuse known result to predict; verify by multiplication.

y-m-41-06.title: Two friends disagree about inverse of AB
y-m-41-06.topic: Inverse of product: order of inverse multiplication
y-m-41-06.goal: Use one example to compare formulas; distinguish what it can show; explain general order with symbols.
y-m-41-06.material: A rows (1,2),(0,1), B rows (1,0),(3,1), both invertible. A⁻¹ rows (1,−2),(0,1); B⁻¹ rows (1,0),(−3,1). AB rows (7,2),(3,1). Haeun says inverse AB=A⁻¹ then B⁻¹; Doyun says B⁻¹ then A⁻¹. Call Haeun result X rows (7,−2),(−3,1); Doyun result Y rows (1,−2),(−3,7). [1 2 0 1 1 0 3 1 1 2 0 1 1 0 3 1 7 2 3 1 7 2 3 1 1 2 3 7]

y-m-41-06.s.s1.r.c: Check all four entries of (AB)X to see if identity.

y-m-41-06.s.s3.model.0: (AB)(B⁻¹A⁻¹)=A(BB⁻¹)A⁻¹=AEA⁻¹=AA⁻¹=E, so B⁻¹A⁻¹ is inverse of AB. B and B⁻¹ meet inside first, so order reverses.
y-m-41-06.s.s3.model.1: Multiply B⁻¹ on right of AB to cancel B, then A⁻¹ to cancel A; identity remains. Thus B inverse first, A inverse after.
y-m-41-06.s.s3.model.2: Inverse gives identity E when multiplied. Inverse of AB is B⁻¹ then A⁻¹, so middle factors cancel.
